title: Oven-Roasted Argentinian Lamb Asado
description: A rich, flavorful, and aromatic one-pan dish originating from Argentina, featuring tender lamb, crispy skin, and a creamy side of creme patissiere.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the lamb shoulder, red onion, red bell pepper, red chili pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Transfer the bowl contents to a large Dutch oven or oven-safe skillet, and drizzle with olive oil.
Roast for 3 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the skin is crispy.

While the lamb is roasting, prepare the creme patissiere. In a medium saucepan, combine the milk, heavy cream, eggs, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Whisk until smooth, then cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the Dutch oven from the oven, and carefully transfer the lamb to a cutting board. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, discarding the solids.
Bring the cooking liquid to a simmer over medium heat, and cook until reduced by half. Stir in the flour to thicken the sauce.
Return the lamb to the Dutch oven, and spoon some of the cooking sauce over the top.
Reheat the creme patissiere in the microwave or on the stovetop, and serve alongside the lamb.
Garnish with fresh herbs, if desired.
Let the dish rest for 15 minutes before slicing and serving.
Reheat any leftovers in the oven with a bit of additional butter and creme patissiere, if desired.
